title: Working mechanisms in the longitudinal study of psychotherapy in aging
summary: This study focuses on identifying the mechanisms underlying psychotherapy for older adults. While the effectiveness of psychotherapy in later life has been well established, little is known about how psychotherapy works in this population. In particular, we are interested in the extent to which psychotherapy can reduce stress in older adults. To this end, we aim to examine how the stress experience changes before, during, and after psychotherapy sessions.
conditions: Mental and behavioural disorders (Chapter V, F00–F99)

interventions.name: Patients at the psychotherapy outpatient clinic for older adults provide saliva samples before and after each therapy session for the analysis of physiological stress markers. In addition, they complete self-report measures assessing subjective stress experience and perceived therapy mechanisms.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients of the psychotherapy outpatient clinic for older adults
Exclusion criteria:
Concerning physiological stress markers: use of medications with strong endocrine, autonomic, or immunological effects (e.g., corticosteroids).
